This page lists my peer-reviewed articles, manuscripts under review, conference papers and presentations. Most of this work estimates how common infectious diseases are in Bangladeshi dairy herds when diagnostic tests are imperfect, what drives infection, how it spreads with age and time, and what it costs farmers.

The diseases covered include brucellosis, paratuberculosis, Q fever (*Coxiella burnetii*), neosporosis, bovine viral diarrhoea, subclinical mastitis and fascioliasis. The main methods are Bayesian latent-class models, hierarchical catalytic (force-of-infection) models, mixture models for diagnostic cut-offs, mixed-effects regression and decision-analytic economic models.

My role on each paper is noted below the reference.
